title: Description of input and examples for PHREEQC version 3 - a computer program for speciation, batch-reaction, one-dimensional transport, and inverse geochemical calculations (Example 8: surface complexation of zinc on hydrous ferric oxide)
journal: U.S. Geological Survey Techniques and Methods, book 6, chap. A43
water_body: synthetic 0.1 mol/kgw NaNO3 solution (no natural water)
alkalinity: none (closed system, no CO2; pH fixed with NaOH)
location_in_paper: Example 8; reference selected-output file ex8.sel (PHREEQC distribution, usgs-coupled/phreeqc3 examples/ex8.sel), rows 'react', soln 1
notes: Total Zn 1e-07 mol/kgw; dissolved Zn = total - sorbed; least-squares slope of log10 values on pH at 0.25-pH steps 6.5-8.0. Two-site diffuse-layer (Dzombak & Morel-type) model with Example-8 constants (pKa1 7.18, pKa2 8.82; Zn log K 0.66 strong, -2.32 weak; these differ from the D&M 1990 best estimates 0.99/-1.99 carried in phreeqc.dat). HFO 0.09 g/kgw (about 1e-3 mol Fe), 5e-6 mol strong + 2e-4 mol weak sites, 600 m2/g, I = 0.1. Lab-type sorbent excess, so the edge is far steeper than in natural waters (compare models_own_slopes.csv). Slope computed by this study from the tabulated model output; not a natural water. Curve is not linear over the window (edge), r reported is Pearson on log10 values.

title: The distribution and behaviour of Fe, Al, Si, Mn, Cu and Ni in ombrotrophic tropical peat draining blackwater estuaries on Borneo Island
journal: Frontiers in Marine Science 9 (article 1075155; volume year 2022, published 9 Jan 2023)
water_body: Maludam and Sebuyau rivers and estuaries (blackwater, peat-draining)
measure: other (Visual MINTEQ 3.0 NICA-Donnan modelled percent of dissolved metal bound to DOM)
location_in_paper: Results text accompanying Fig. 8; Table 3 (NICA constants)
notes: Quoted: 'We calculated 100% Fe and 98-100% Cu bound to DOM in Maludam, and 70-100% Fe and 96-100% Cu bound to DOM in Sebuyau river and estuaries.' and 'The percentage of Fe and Cu bound to DOM at pH 3.3 - 6 varied (70-100%), however, at higher pH (> 6) it became stable at 90-100%.' Implies the modelled non-DOM (inorganic) Cu fraction is small (<= 4%) and least variable above pH 6; no slope given; salinity co-varies with pH along the estuaries. Generic FA constants listed in Table 3 for Cu (n1 0.63, log K2 7.26 as printed) differ from those reproduced by Xu et al. 2016 (n1 0.53, log K2 8.26).
